seo_title: AdSense Not Approved? Fix Every Rejection Reason (2026 Guide)
description: Rejected by AdSense? This step-by-step guide decodes every official rejection reason, fixes the content, ads.txt, privacy policy and technical issues that actually cause it, and gives you a 14-day plan to get approved — sourced directly to Google's own AdSense Help documentation.

faq: Why was my AdSense application rejected with no clear reason given?

A vague rejection email almost always has a more specific reason sitting in your AdSense account's Policy Center, under Sites. Google's automated review increasingly logs the actual issue there — low value content, a policy violation, or a technical crawlability problem — even when the email itself just says the site isn't ready. Check the Policy Center before assuming which category applies, since guessing wrong means you spend days fixing something that was never the actual problem.
How long does AdSense review actually take?

Google does not publish a fixed timeline, and review happens in stages — an automated pass first, then sometimes a more thorough human review — so the honest answer is that it varies genuinely by site and by how much the automated stage needs to escalate. Some applicants hear back within a couple of days; others wait considerably longer. There is no official number to count down to, and no evidence that contacting Google to ask for status speeds anything up.
How many times can I reapply after a rejection?

There's no published cap on the number of applications. What matters is that each reapplication reflects genuine, verifiable changes from the version of the site that was rejected — reapplying the same day with nothing changed wastes a review cycle without addressing anything, and repeated rejections for the identical unaddressed reason are a worse pattern than a single first rejection. Fix the issue properly, wait a week or two, then reapply.
Does my domain need to be a certain age before AdSense will approve it?

No. Google has never published a minimum domain age requirement. What actually correlates with age is content volume and search indexation — an older domain has often simply had more time to accumulate substantial content and organic links, which are the real factors under review. A brand-new domain with genuinely strong, original content is not disqualified by its age alone, and plenty of new domains are approved within weeks of registration.
Is there a minimum traffic requirement to get approved?

No official minimum traffic threshold exists anywhere in Google's published eligibility documentation. What matters is that your content is substantial, original, policy-compliant, and reachable by a crawler — not that a specific number of people have already visited before you apply. A site with modest but genuine traffic is in a stronger position than a site with inflated numbers from a traffic exchange or purchased visitors, which creates an invalid-traffic problem rather than helping.
I already have a Privacy Policy page — why was I still rejected for policy compliance?

A Privacy Policy generated from a generic template and never edited often fails to actually say anything relevant to your site — it may never mention that you use cookies, run third-party advertising, or name AdSense specifically, and it may still contain placeholder text or clauses copied from an unrelated business type. A policy that will hold up needs to name your site, disclose AdSense and cookie use explicitly, and cover GDPR or CCPA rights if applicable to your visitors.
What is ads.txt and can a missing one really cause a rejection?

Ads.txt is a plain text file at your domain's true root that authorizes AdSense to sell your site's advertising inventory, protecting against a category of ad fraud. A missing file, a file with a placeholder publisher ID never replaced with the real one, or a file placed in the wrong location can all be flagged during review, and it produces no visible symptom on the site itself — everything looks completely normal to you as a visitor while it silently affects your application.
Can I use a free subdomain like Blogspot or WordPress.com and still get approved?

It's not impossible, but ownership verification can behave differently on a shared platform domain than it does on a domain you own and control outright, since AdSense needs to associate the account with a property you fully control. Where possible, applying with a domain you own directly removes this friction entirely and also gives you full control over ads.txt, robots.txt, and site structure that a shared platform partially restricts.
Is it safe to pay a service that guarantees AdSense approval?

No third party can guarantee an outcome that only Google's own review process determines, and any service claiming otherwise should be treated with real skepticism. At best, such services charge a markup to apply the same content and technical fixes covered in a guide like this one; at worst, they use traffic-inflation or content practices that create exactly the invalid-traffic and policy problems that cause rejections, leaving the site worse off than before you paid.
Does using AI to help write my content automatically disqualify me from AdSense?

No. AI-assisted writing is not against AdSense policy on its own, and plenty of approved sites use AI tools somewhere in their workflow. What gets flagged is content that reads as generic and unedited, interchangeable with countless other sites answering the same prompt with the same structure. The fix is adding what only you can add — your own examples, your own tested results, your own specific opinion — not avoiding AI assistance entirely.
My site was rejected twice for the exact same reason — what am I missing?

The most likely explanation is that the first fix was partial rather than complete: a few thin pages expanded out of many that needed it, an ads.txt file added but still carrying the wrong publisher ID, a Privacy Policy edited on the surface but still generic underneath. Go back through the specific checklist for that rejection category rather than assuming the label alone tells you everything, and verify each item with the diagnostic checks described rather than a quick glance.
What's the difference between a rejection and my account showing "Getting ready"?

A rejection means the site didn't clear the baseline review. "Getting ready" is a different, more advanced state — it means baseline eligibility already passed and Google is now serving a limited number of ads on the site to further evaluate its suitability before granting full approval. If you see this status, the right response is continued normal publishing rather than the rejection fix list, though the same underlying quality bar applies to both situations.
Can I run another ad network while I wait to reapply to AdSense?

Yes — running an alternative ad network or pursuing direct sponsorships while you fix your site for AdSense doesn't violate AdSense's own policies, since you don't have an active AdSense account serving ads yet. Check each specific alternative network's own exclusivity terms before switching later, since some require removing their ads before AdSense can run alongside them, but there's no rule against monetizing through a legitimate alternative during the gap.
Will a rejection permanently block my domain from ever being approved?

No. A standard content or readiness rejection is designed as a "not yet," not a permanent ban, and sites that address the actual issue and reapply are routinely approved afterward — that's the entire premise of this guide. This is different from an account suspension for a serious policy violation after approval, which is a separate and more serious outcome with its own appeals process, but a first-time application rejection does not carry that weight.
Should I completely redesign my site before reapplying?

Not on its own. Visual design is essentially unrelated to the documented rejection categories — content substance, policy compliance, navigation, and technical crawlability. A striking redesign built on top of the same thin content or the same missing ads.txt file changes nothing about the actual issue. Spend the time on the substantive fixes in this guide first; a design refresh is worth doing eventually, but it won't move a rejected application on its own.

Tags play a minor, supporting role. YouTube has said tags are useful mainly when your topic is commonly misspelled. Titles, thumbnails, the first two lines of your description and actual viewer satisfaction carry far more weight, so fix those before you spend an hour writing tags.
How long does it take for a video to rank in YouTube search?

Search rankings usually settle within two to six weeks, but evergreen videos keep climbing for months as watch time accumulates. Judge a search-intent video on its 90-day impressions curve, not its first 48 hours.
Should I change the title of a video that is not ranking?
Yes, if the video has impressions but a weak click-through rate, or if it is ranking for the wrong query. Change one variable at a time and give it 14 days before you judge the result.

YouTube states that half of all channels and videos have an impressions CTR between 2% and 10%. A brand-new channel often sits lower because most impressions come from cold browse traffic; a channel with loyal subscribers can exceed 10% simply because its audience recognises the name.
Why does my CTR drop when a video goes viral?

That is normal and usually healthy. As YouTube pushes a video to broader, colder audiences the denominator (impressions) grows much faster than clicks. Falling CTR alongside rising total views is a sign of expanding reach, not failure.
Does changing a thumbnail reset a video's performance?
No. Swapping a thumbnail does not reset the video or remove it from recommendations. YouTube keeps serving impressions and you can compare the before/after period in the Content tab of Analytics.

Yes, in eligible countries. Does watch time from private or unlisted videos count?
No. Only valid public watch hours count toward the threshold. Watch time from videos you later delete, make private, or that are removed for policy violations is not counted.
Why was my monetization application rejected for reused content?

YouTube requires that you add significant original commentary, editing or educational value. Compilations, reaction videos with minimal input, and re-uploaded clips are the most common rejection reasons under the channel monetization policies.

faq: What is the difference between CPM and RPM?

CPM is what advertisers pay per thousand ad impressions before YouTube's share. RPM is your estimated earnings per thousand video views after the revenue split and including views that carried no ads. RPM is always lower than CPM, and RPM is the number that matters to you.
How much of ad revenue does YouTube pay creators?

For watch page ads on long-form videos, YouTube pays creators 55% of net ad revenue. For Shorts feed ads the allocation works differently: revenue enters a Creator Pool and monetizing creators receive 45% of their allocated share after music licensing costs.
Does making longer videos increase RPM?

It can, because videos over roughly eight minutes are eligible for mid-roll ads, which raises the number of ad impressions per view. But padding a five-minute idea to eight minutes usually hurts retention enough to cancel out the gain.

Not to start. YouTube's own search suggestions, the Research tab in YouTube Studio, Google Trends and your existing traffic-source report cover most of what a small channel needs. Paid tools mainly save time on competition scoring once you publish weekly.
How do I know if a keyword is too competitive?
Search it and read the first six results. If every one comes from a channel with more than ten times your subscriber count, and the videos are recent and thorough, pick a narrower variant instead.
Should every video target a keyword?
No. Roughly half your catalogue should target search intent and half should target browse and suggested traffic. Search-led videos build a compounding library; browse-led videos build an audience.

faq: Do high CPC keywords in the title raise my ad rates?

Not directly. Advertisers bid on audiences and topics, not on the literal words in your title. What raises your rates is producing content that genuinely attracts viewers advertisers want — typically people close to a purchase decision.
Which YouTube niches have the highest CPMs?

Personal finance, investing, insurance, B2B software, legal and real estate consistently sit at the top because a single converted customer is worth hundreds or thousands of dollars. Gaming, vlogs and entertainment sit at the bottom for the opposite reason.
Is it worth switching niches purely for higher CPM?
Rarely. A finance channel you have no interest in will stall long before the RPM advantage matters. A better move is finding the highest-value sub-topic inside a niche you can sustain for years.

faq: What is the single most important YouTube metric?

Average view duration relative to video length, combined with click-through rate. Together they tell you whether the packaging attracted the right people and whether the content kept them. Views alone tell you nothing about why.
How many impressions does a video need before the data is meaningful?
As a rule of thumb, wait for at least 1,000 impressions before drawing conclusions about CTR, and 48 to 72 hours before comparing retention against your channel average.
Why do returning viewers matter more than subscribers?

Subscriber count is a vanity number once a channel is a few years old; many subscribers never return. The returning-viewers figure in the Audience tab shows how many real people came back this month, which is a far better predictor of stable revenue.

faq: Does the YouTube algorithm punish channels for uploading inconsistently?

There is no penalty for an irregular schedule. What actually happens is that fewer recent uploads means fewer chances to be recommended, and a dormant audience clicks less when you return. The effect looks like a penalty but is really lost momentum.
Do the first 24 hours decide a video's fate?

For browse-driven videos, early signals matter a lot. For search-driven videos they barely matter — evergreen tutorials routinely find their audience weeks or months after upload as they accumulate search rankings.
How should I respond to an algorithm update?
Check whether the drop is concentrated in one traffic source before changing anything. A fall in browse traffic with stable search traffic is a packaging or freshness issue, not a sitewide penalty.

Three to five is plenty: one channel roughly your size, two a tier above, and one outside your niche whose format you admire. More than that and the patterns blur together.
Is it legal to use a competitor's tags?

Tags are public metadata and using similar tags is not a violation. What you cannot do is copy their thumbnails, scripts or footage, which is a copyright issue and a monetization risk under the reused content policy.
How often should I redo a competitor teardown?
Once a quarter. Doing it more often leads to reactive, imitative content; doing it less means you miss format shifts that spread through a niche in a matter of months.

Do comments count more than likes?

For your media kit they weigh the same, but for the recommendation system a comment is a much stronger signal of investment. A video with an unusually high comment-to-view ratio is a format worth repeating.
Should I include Shorts in my engagement rate?
Report them separately. Shorts generate huge view counts with proportionally fewer likes and comments, so blending them into one figure understates your long-form engagement and confuses sponsors.

How specific should a target audience be?

Specific enough that you can name a real person who fits it and predict what they would search this week. “Self-taught developers in their first six months of job hunting” is workable; “programmers” is not.
Does a narrow audience limit growth?
In the early years it accelerates it. A narrow audience produces higher retention and stronger engagement signals, which is exactly what pushes a video into broader recommendation surfaces later.

Why is my CPM high but my earnings low?
CPM counts only monetized playbacks and sits before YouTube's share. If only a third of your views carried an ad, your RPM will be a fraction of your CPM even though nothing is wrong.
When does AdSense pay out?
Earnings are finalised in the first half of the following month and paid once your balance passes the payment threshold, provided your payment details and tax information are verified.

How many views do I need before a digital product is worth making?
As a rough guide, 10,000 monthly views on topic-relevant videos. Below that, the conversion volume rarely justifies weeks of production time — affiliate links are the better first step.
Do I have to disclose affiliate links?
Yes. The FTC requires clear and conspicuous disclosure of material connections, and YouTube requires you to declare paid promotions. Put it in the video, not only the description.

How many affiliate links should a description contain?
Link only what you mentioned, in the order you mentioned it, above the fold. A wall of twenty links reads as spam and depresses click-through on all of them.
Can affiliate links get a video demonetized?

Not by themselves. Problems arise when you fail to disclose the relationship, link to prohibited products, or use misleading claims — all of which are covered by YouTube's advertiser-friendly guidelines and FTC rules.

Do I have to declare a paid promotion to YouTube?
Yes. Tick the paid promotion box in Studio and state the sponsorship verbally in the video. Both YouTube's policy and FTC guidance require clear disclosure that viewers cannot miss.

Neither bans AI assistance outright. Google's guidance judges content on quality and usefulness rather than production method, while YouTube requires disclosure of realistic synthetic media. Fully automated, low-value content is what gets penalised.

A raw transcript pasted alone adds little value and may be judged thin. A transcript restructured into a proper article with headings, context and extra detail is treated as ordinary content.
How long before a new site gets organic traffic?
Expect three to nine months of near-zero traffic on a fresh domain, then a compounding curve. Publish the pages that will still be relevant in two years first.

Between 0.5% and 3% of views for a relevant free resource. Anything above 3% usually means the offer is unusually well matched to the video topic.

Both, with different jobs. Shorts are the cheapest way to get discovered; long-form is where watch time, ad revenue and genuine loyalty are built. Shorts that never lead anywhere are a treadmill.

Why did my revenue drop in January?

faq: What makes a camera good for videography?
High-quality recording formats (10-bit, less compression), log profiles, no recording limits, professional audio inputs, video-focused controls and reliable autofocus.
Do I need raw video for YouTube?
Rarely. Raw creates huge files and long workflows. 10-bit log or a good standard profile is enough for most YouTube work.
Should I buy a cinema camera or mirrorless?
For most YouTube creators a hybrid or video-focused mirrorless camera is the practical choice. Cinema cameras suit rigged productions and film work.

Handles must be between 3 and 30 characters and can include letters, numbers, underscores, hyphens and full stops.

Yes. If a verified channel changes its name, the verification badge is removed and you need to reapply.
Should my handle match my channel name?
Ideally yes, or as closely as possible, so viewers can find you and impersonation is harder.

Can I add trending keywords my video doesn't cover?

faq: Which YouTube statistic matters most?
There is no single one. Impressions and CTR show packaging; retention and average view duration show whether the video delivers.
Can I see another channel's statistics?
Only public ones: views, likes (unless hidden), comments, and metadata. Impressions, retention and revenue are private.
What is a good CTR on YouTube?
It depends on niche, traffic source and channel size. Compare against your own typical performance in Studio.

faq: What is the difference between a target market and target audience?
The market is the broad pool of people and money in your topic; the audience is the specific viewer each video or series is made for.
How do I find my YouTube target audience?
Start with a hypothesis, then validate it with YouTube Analytics audience reports, search terms and comments.
Does a narrow audience limit growth?
Usually not. Specific videos are easier to recommend, and excellent videos reach beyond the core audience.

A company-controlled Google account, with at least two trusted owners and everyone else on lower roles.
What content works best for business channels?
Educational how-to videos, product tutorials, customer stories and thought leadership — help first, sell second.

faq: What is the average CPM on YouTube?
YouTube doesn't publish one. Many long-form channels see roughly $2–$12, with high-value niches and audiences far higher.
Why is my RPM lower than my CPM?
CPM is before YouTube's share and counts only monetized playbacks; RPM is after the share and counts all views.
When is YouTube CPM highest?
Usually October to December, with January typically the lowest month.

They define how the brand can use your content — where, for how long, in which territories and whether as paid ads.

faq: How do you calculate YouTube earnings?
Views divided by 1,000, multiplied by RPM — calculated separately for long-form and Shorts.
Why are online earnings estimates so wide?
They apply one generic rate to every channel, ignoring niche, geography, Shorts and non-ad income.
Is ad revenue most of a creator's income?
Often not. Sponsorships, affiliates and products can exceed ad revenue, especially for mid-sized channels.

Can I add other creators' videos to my playlist?
